input.title: ZM3D playable: brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable: brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies). Written 1 Oct 2025 by Julia Lawson for the build PlayableX are starting with us on Monday 3 November 2025.

This is written for the game as it plays today. We are looking at a change to the core gameplay. If it goes ahead, we will redo the affected parts of this brief with you in November.

1. Scenario and what it is for
We picked Scenario 1: the core game in its simplest form, with no extra framing or character story. The playable is there to give a clean first read of the real mechanic. Players who like it should go on to like the game, and players who won't like the game should drop out at the ad, not after installing. So keep it true to the game rather than tuning it for the cheapest install.
The player picks any items they like from the board and can make as many matches as their skill allows. It is not on rails like the Domino Delights playable.

2. The board: eight items
These eight are the default board:
1. Grenade (powerful)
2. Couch (splash damage)
3. Plushie Chick (weak but funny; this is the item you called "the duck" in the reference level)
4. Shuriken
5. Cute Axe
6. Gift Box
7. Cactus Plant
8. Bow
Grenade, Couch and Plushie Chick are carried over from the reference level. The other five are Robert's picks. Bow replaces Dynamite, which was on his first list. Bow comes as it is today, without an arrow. The arrow may become its own item later.
Extras: every other board item on our pack list is an extra you can swap in on the board, including Dynamite, Couch and Pillow and Plushie Bunny from the reference level. The hand-off list (linked below) marks each item Default or Extra.

3. Zombies and animation
Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player.
One animation: walk.
All four are in the Unity package Marcus sent on 26 September, which you have already reviewed. You told us you will re-rig them in Spine and rebuild the animation from the Unity keyframes, and that more zombies can come later depending on size.

4. How a level plays
Items sit in a 3D physics pile and the player taps them into a tray at the bottom.
Tray: 7 slots. Any 3 matching items in the tray clear, and each cleared triple fires that item at the zombies.
Different items hit differently (for example, Grenade is powerful, Couch does splash damage and Plushie Chick is weak). That difference is the point we want players to notice.
If all 7 slots fill with no match, that counts as a blunder. The tray clears and the surviving zombies enrage, but play goes on. A full tray is a tempo penalty, not a loss.
Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
Lose: the zombies reach the player and the player's HP runs out. This is the only fail state.
Reference: the reference level Brian recorded and sent you on 24 September shows what we built for you (background, cannon/"rocket launcher" with its projectile, and the win/lose flow). Its board item set differs from the eight above. The eight above win.

5. Sound
We only hand over sound that is ours to hand over.
Ours, and coming to you as .wav: Matching sound, Success sound, Failure sound.
Background music: a new track made by us for the ad (not the in-game music). Calvin is still cutting it down to a loop, so it is still owed.
Rocket sound and Explosion sound: the in-game versions come from a sound library and a bought sound pack. They stay with us, and we will send our own versions once Calvin has made them. Until then, please treat both as owed and do not source replacements on our behalf.
Music start: as with Domino Delights, the music starts only after the player's first tap, and so does the timer.

6. Formats
Your format list still holds:
3D: .fbx, .glb or .blend. For .fbx, Binary only, never ASCII.
2D: .png. For 2D animation, character parts are separated into pieces.
Font: .ttf or .woff2.
Sound: .mp3 or .wav.

7. Start date
Kickoff and build start: Monday 3 November 2025, 9:00-9:30 am Pacific (17:00 UTC).

8. What is still coming from us
The hand-off list (Google Sheet, linked in our message) has one row per line of our pack list. Each row shows its state:
Delivered: you already have the current file.
Ready: in our outgoing folder, in a format you take, current, and nobody is changing it.
Owed: still to come, with what is owed and who has it.
As of 1 October: 8 Delivered, 36 Ready, 52 Owed. Of the default eight, one is still owed: Cactus Plant, which gets re-exported with its new colour versions.

Contacts on our side: Frederick Stone (producer), Julia Lawson (design), Brian Foster (assets), Robert (product).

input.message:
Done. The brief and hand-off list are in my Drive, view-only for you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake.
• Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c9fe5bf6d75945bd03ab96c/edit
• Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1J9sYfM4nrcoL5FzKGoiVp8oAPXs-iswWbfLrOcrkF88/edit

*Count by state (96 lines):* Delivered 8 · Ready 36 · Owed 52

Owed by who has it: Brian 25 · Claire 22 · Calvin 3 · Martin 1. All 52 tickets are now in Todo with a comment, and Delivered/Ready are untouched.

Things that override Brian's ticket notes:
• The 12 models Brian saved out of Unity on 25 Sep (3 living room, 9 kitchen) are ASCII FBX, per Marcus on 26 Sep. PlayableX take Binary only, so those all need re-exporting.
• The 8 instruments zip got cut off on upload (Brian's folder log, 30 Sep), so they aren't in the outgoing folder.
• Claire is redoing the bathroom UVs, so the 12 bathroom files from Friday are the old version.
• Cactus, Chainsaw and Cone got new colour versions on 29 Sep, after they were exported, so they go again.
• Rocket and Explosion sounds come from Soundly and an Asset Store pack. They stay with us until Calvin makes our own.
• Robert moved Bow into the 8 in place of Dynamite on 26 Sep. Of the board 8: 3 are Delivered, 4 are Ready, and Cactus is Owed.

Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, ahead of the 3 November start, here is what you'll build from and where our assets stand:
• *Brief:* https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c9fe5bf6d75945bd03ab96c/edit
• *Hand-off list:* https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1J9sYfM4nrcoL5FzKGoiVp8oAPXs-iswWbfLrOcrkF88/edit

The brief has the scenario (1, the core game), the 8 board items, and the 4 zombies with the walk animation. It also covers the win/lose rules, the 7-slot tray, sound (music starts after the first tap, like last time) and the start date. The list has one row per asset, each marked Delivered, Ready or Owed. The Owed rows (52 of 96 right now) are what's still coming from us, and each one says what's missing. It's written for the game as it is today. If our core gameplay changes, we'll go through the affected parts with you in November. Both are shared with intake@playablex.ai as well.

Correction to the split above: it's Brian 27 · Claire 21 · Calvin 3 · Martin 1, which still adds up to 52 Owed. The state counts (8 / 36 / 52) are right, and the sheet has the correct owner on every row.
